jobs.title: Sr. Clinical Research Associate - Early Phase Studies (Las Vegas, NV)
jobs.description:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

Job Description

Join Us as a Clinical Research Associate – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation

We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years.

As part of our global Early Development team, you'll have the opportunity to support complex, early-phase clinical trials that advance innovative therapies through critical stages of drug development.

As a Clinical Research Associate (CRA) supporting Early Development studies, you will independently perform and coordinate clinical monitoring and site management activities, with a focus on Phase I and clinical pharmacology studies. You'll conduct on-site visits to assess protocol compliance, participant safety, data integrity, and regulatory adherence.

This position will primarily support an investigational site in Las Vegas, Nevada, and candidates must be based in the Las Vegas area.

While the primary focus will be the Las Vegas site, travel to additional investigational sites in other locations may be required based on business and study needs.

This role requires strong clinical knowledge, independent monitoring expertise, and an understanding of the unique complexities of early-phase research, including intensive safety assessments, dose escalation, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) sampling, and time-sensitive study procedures.

Acting as a site processes specialist, you will ensure that clinical trials are conducted in accordance with approved protocols, ICH-GCP guidelines, applicable regulations, and standard operating procedures (SOPs), while safeguarding participant rights, safety, and well-being. You will also ensure audit readiness and develop collaborative relationships with investigational sites, sponsors, and cross-functional study teams.

What You'll Do

• Independently monitor investigational sites using a risk-based monitoring approach, applying critical thinking, root cause analysis, and problem-solving skills to identify compliance gaps, mitigate risks, and implement corrective and preventive actions.
• Conduct site qualification visits, site initiation visits (SIVs), interim monitoring visits (IMVs), and close-out visits (COVs) in accordance with approved monitoring plans, study protocols, and applicable regulatory requirements.
• Support Phase I and Early Development studies, including complex clinical pharmacology protocols such as First-in-Human (FIH), Single Ascending Dose (SAD), Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD), and PK/PD studies.
• Monitor early-phase study activities with particular attention to participant safety, dose escalation procedures, protocol-defined stopping criteria, dosing requirements, time-sensitive sample collection, and intensive clinical data review.
• Perform source data review (SDR), source data verification (SDV), and case report form (CRF) review, as applicable, to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and protocol compliance. Review relevant clinical documentation, including medical histories, laboratory results, concomitant medications, adverse events, and eligibility assessments.
• Assess investigational product accountability through physical inventory and records review, ensuring compliance with protocol-specific dosing and administration requirements.
• Identify, document, and escalate safety concerns, protocol deviations, data discrepancies, and other study risks in a timely manner. Partner with investigational sites and project teams to ensure appropriate resolution and follow-up.
• Document monitoring observations through timely, accurate reports and follow-up letters in accordance with approved business writing standards.
• Maintain regular communication with investigational sites between monitoring visits to confirm protocol adherence, resolution of outstanding issues, and timely data entry.
• Participate in investigator meetings and collaborate with sponsors and internal teams to support site identification, qualification, initiation, ongoing monitoring, and study close-out activities.
• Ensure essential documents are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and project requirements. Conduct on-site file reviews as required.
• Maintain accurate and timely study tracking, monitoring documentation, and updates within clinical trial management systems (CTMS) and other applicable platforms.
• Facilitate effective communication among investigational sites, sponsors, and cross-functional study teams, particularly regarding time-sensitive clinical activities and emerging study risks.
• Support audit and inspection readiness and respond to applicable sponsor, company, and regulatory requirements.
• Maintain administrative responsibilities, including expense reports, timesheets, and other required documentation.
• Contribute to project initiatives, process improvements, and knowledge sharing across the clinical operations team. May provide guidance or mentoring to less experienced CRAs as appropriate.

Education and Experience Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in life sciences, nursing, pharmacy, or a related medical/scientific discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.
• 3-5+ years of independent clinical monitoring experience as a CRA, including demonstrated experience conducting site qualification, initiation, interim monitoring, and close-out visits.
• Previous Phase I / Early Development clinical monitoring experience is strongly preferred, particularly experience supporting complex early-phase or clinical pharmacology studies. Approximately 3+ years of Phase I monitoring experience is ideal; however, candidates with less Phase I experience and substantial hands-on exposure to complex early-phase protocols will also be considered.
• Direct monitoring experience with multiple early-phase study designs is highly preferred, particularly First-in-Human (FIH), Single Ascending Dose (SAD), and Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) studies. Experience with PK/PD, Drug-Drug Interaction (DDI), Food Effect, or Bioavailability/Bioequivalence (BA/BE) studies is also valuable.
• Strong medical and scientific knowledge, with demonstrated ability to independently review and interpret clinical source documentation, including medical histories, laboratory results, concomitant medications, adverse events, and eligibility criteria.
• Must be based in the Las Vegas, NV area to support the primary investigational site, with flexibility to travel to additional locations as needed.
• Valid driver's license where applicable.

An equivalency consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training, and directly related experience may be considered sufficient to meet applicable educational requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

The following experience is highly desirable and may differentiate candidates:

• Experience monitoring additional clinical pharmacology studies, including QT/QTc, ADME/mass balance, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, MASH, or other specialty-population studies.
• Experience supporting studies involving complex routes of administration, including intravenous (IV), subcutaneous (SC), or other injectable therapies.
• Previous monitoring experience within dedicated Phase I units or clinical pharmacology units.
• Experience serving as a Lead CRA, mentoring junior CRAs, or assuming additional senior-level monitoring responsibilities.
• Experience working independently within lean or cross-functional project structures, including studies without a designated Clinical Trial Manager (CTM).

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Strong clinical and medical terminology knowledge, including the ability to review complex clinical data and identify potential safety, eligibility, and protocol compliance concerns.
• Thorough understanding of ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, SOPs, and clinical monitoring requirements.
• Strong understanding of early-phase clinical trial conduct, including dose escalation, intensive safety monitoring, stopping criteria, dosing procedures, PK/PD sampling requirements, and high-volume source data review.
• Demonstrated ability to independently manage monitoring activities, prioritize competing study requirements, and exercise sound clinical judgment.
• Well-developed critical thinking, risk assessment, root cause analysis, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and escalate issues appropriately.
• Strong understanding of risk-based monitoring concepts and processes.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with investigational sites, medical personnel, sponsors, and cross-functional project teams.
• Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills, with a customer-focused approach.
• Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced, time-sensitive clinical research environments.
• Ability to work independently with minimal oversight while contributing effectively to collaborative study teams.
• Flexibility and adaptability to changing study priorities, operational needs, and complex clinical scenarios.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to learn and effectively utilize clinical trial management systems and other relevant software.
• Strong English language and grammar skills.

Working Conditions and Environment

• Location Requirement: Candidates must be based in the Las Vegas, NV area, as this position will primarily support an investigational site in that location.
• Travel: Regular travel to the primary Las Vegas investigational site is required, with potential travel to additional sites in other locations based on study assignments and business needs. Overnight travel may be required.
• Work is performed in an office, laboratory, clinical, and/or home office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment.
• Potential exposure to biological fluids and infectious organisms in clinical environments.
• Personal protective equipment, including protective eyewear, garments, and gloves, may be required.
• Rare exposure to fluctuating and/or extreme temperatures.

jobs.title: STAGE 2027 - Ingénieur Hygiène, Sécurité et Environnement (ALL GENDER)
jobs.description:
Job Description:

En quête d’une première expérience qui fait la différence ?

Rejoins Airbus Atlantic et donne une trajectoire unique à ton parcours grâce à ce stage.

Nous sommes un leader mondial sur le marché des aérostructures, des sièges pilotes et des fauteuils passagers premium.

Dans le cadre de votre formation initiale, vous recherchez un stage obligatoire ou intégré dans une année de césure, d’une durée de 4 à 6 mois, vous permettant de valider votre année.

Une offre de stage intitulée « STAGE 2027 - Ingénieur Hygiène, Sécurité et Environnement (ALL GENDER) » vient de s'ouvrir au sein d’Airbus Atlantic sur le site de Rochefort.

Cette mission débutera en janvier 2027 (date sujette à flexibilité) pour une durée de 6 mois.

Découvrez le site en vidéo :

Présentation Airbus Atlantic

Présentation du site de Rochefort

Tâches et responsabilités :

Vous rejoindrez une équipe de 2 personnes au sein du département « Hygiène, Sécurité et Environnement (HSE) » en charge de maîtriser les risques liés aux activités de la l’entreprise pour protéger la santé des salariés, sécuriser les installations et réduire l’impact écologique.

Encadré par votre tuteur, vous interviendrez sur les activités suivantes :

• Évaluation des risques & Conformité : Réaliser l'évaluation des risques liés aux équipements de protection (EPI) sur le centre de formation, conduire la veille réglementaire associée et formaliser les plans d'action correctifs dans le document unique.
• Ingénierie pédagogique & Sensibilisation : Concevoir, tester et déployer des modules de sensibilisation interactifs aux risques HSE, adaptés aux contraintes opérationnelles des équipes.
• Audit & Amélioration continue : Participer à la réalisation d'audits terrain HSE, analyser les écarts et proposer des outils visuels et indicateurs permettant de redynamiser l'engagement des collaborateurs.
• Mise à jour documentaire : Piloter la révision des procédures et consignes de sécurité du site pour en garantir la conformité et la lisibilité.

Durant votre stage, vous développerez les compétences suivantes en lien avec votre formation :

• Conformité & Analyse des risques : Maîtrise des audits de conformité, mise à jour des documents réglementaires et évaluation méthodologique des risques sur le terrain.
• Gestion de projet HSE : Pilotage d'actions de prévention de leur phase de cadrage jusqu'à la mesure de leur impact.
• Ingénierie pédagogique & Communication : Conception de modules de sensibilisation interactifs et animation de rituels sécurité pour engager le personnel.

Parlons de VOUS !

Vous préparez actuellement un diplôme de niveau Bac +4 ou Bac +5 (ou équivalent) dans le domaine de l’hygiène, de la sécurité et de l’environnement ou une discipline apparentée.

Vous avez les connaissances et compétences suivantes :

• Cadre réglementaire et normes HSE (ISO 14001, ISO 45001), principes d'évaluation des risques professionnels et méthodologies d'audit.
• Maîtrise des techniques de gestion de projet, capacités d'analyse de données de sécurité, ingénierie de formation et maîtrise des outils bureautiques/visuels.
• Savoir être : Curiosité, Esprit d'équipe, Bonne communication, Capacité d'adaptation.
• Anglais : avancé
• Français : courant

Vous pourrez être amené(e) à vous déplacer avec votre tuteur.

Parlons de NOUS !

Rejoindre Airbus Atlantic en tant que stagiaire, c'est :

• Participer à des projets ambitieux, à la pointe de la technologie, visant à construire l’avion de demain tout en répondant aux défis environnementaux,
• Acquérir des compétences dans un environnement dynamique qui encourage la créativité et l'initiative, avec une approche entrepreneuriale,
• Évoluer au sein d'une organisation solidaire, qui valorise la proximité et l'humain.

Notre processus de sélection

Toutes les candidatures seront soigneusement examinées par un recruteur.

Si votre candidature est présélectionnée, vous serez invité à réaliser un entretien vidéo afin de vous présenter.

Après évaluation, les candidats retenus seront contactés pour un entretien avec le manager ou le tuteur qui procédera alors à la sélection finale.
